record.paper_title: Open Problems in Data-Sharing Peer-to-Peer Systems
record.original_question: Can a peer-to-peer search mechanism be built that supports a rich SQL-style query language over decentralized shared data with reasonable performance, and if so what architecture or alternative approach should be used to achieve that performance?

evidence.quote: A great deal of additional research is needed to advance current work into a search mechanism with reasonable performance, and to investigate alternative approaches to the problem.

artifact.status_search_result: No single accepted solution is known to provide full SQL-rich query processing over fully decentralized P2P networks with provably sub-linear performance and complete answers; the topic has been studied (e.g., PIER, Edutella, PeerDB, schema-mediation work) with partial results for restricted query classes, but the general problem as posed remains an open research direction rather than a settled theorem.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in Data-Sharing Peer-to-Peer Systems (zbMATH listing)
status_evidence.snippet: Article identifying open research problems in P2P data sharing including the need for richer query languages with reasonable performance.
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as an open research problem rather than a resolved result.
